findings.summary: Binary vuln_auth_daemon.elf [0x6372]: 1 string(s) matching 'hardcoded_credential' pattern. Examples: ['password=admin_secret_token_2026']

evidence.excerpt: ["password=admin_secret_token_2026"]
String matching hardcoded-credential pattern ('password=') found in binary

advisory.title: Hard-coded credential in binary
advisory.summary: Do not compile secrets into binaries. Read them from environment variables at startup, or fetch them at runtime from a secret manager / key vault (e.g. HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault) with short-lived leases. Rotate the exposed credential immediately and audit its usage history.
advisory.plain_english: A password, token or API key was embedded directly in the binary. Anyone who obtains the file can extract it — strings utilities retrieve embedded secrets in seconds. This finding was CONFIRMED by the Verification Service.
advisory.impact: [severity: medium] Credential theft leading to unauthorised access to the systems or services that accept this secret, and no easy rotation path. The exposed password grants direct login until rotated.
advisory.remediation_patch:
```python
# BEFORE: PASSWORD = "Sup3rS3cret!"   # baked into the file
# AFTER: read from environment or a secret manager
import os
PASSWORD = os.environ.get('APP_PASSWORD')
if not PASSWORD:
    raise RuntimeError('APP_PASSWORD not set; refusing to start')

# Preferred: short-lived lease from a vault
# secret = vault_client.read_latest('kv/credentials/app')
```

advisory.title: Dangerous libc function use in binary
advisory.summary: Replace the unsafe calls: strcpy -> strlcpy/strncpy (or use snprintf), gets -> fgets with an explicit buffer limit, sprintf -> snprintf, strcat -> strlcat/snprintf, and popen/system -> exec-variants that take an argument array after allow-listing the command. Rebuild with warnings (-Wall -Wextra) and compiler hardening (-fstack-protector-strong, FORTIFY_SOURCE) enabled.
advisory.plain_english: The analysed binary contains one or more dangerous libc functions. These functions perform no bounds checking, so an attacker who controls their input can overflow buffers, corrupt memory or execute commands. This finding was CONFIRMED by the Verification Service.
advisory.impact: [severity: high] Buffer overflows leading to crashes (denial of service) or remote code execution with the privileges of the binary.
advisory.threat_vector: Local / Remote Binary Exploitation / Control Flow Hijacking
advisory.verification_test: nm -D target_binary | grep -E '(gets|strcpy|sprintf|system)' || echo 'No unsafe symbols'
